page: Amazon Web Services c9gd.large is a compute-optimized virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a custom AWS Graviton arm64 processor delivering 2 dedicated physical cores running at 3.3 GHz. With a single thread per core, the instance avoids thread contention, offering predictable processing performance for arm64-compatible execution stacks. The instance provides 4.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:2 compute-optimized ratio of 2.0 GB of memory per core.

A key differentiator of the c9gd family is the inclusion of integrated local instance storage. The c9gd.large comes equipped with a 118 GB local NVMe SSD, bypassing network-attached block storage latencies to deliver direct, high-throughput input and output. Networking is configured with a 1 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

From an efficiency perspective, the dedicated arm64 hardware profile offers high power and resource efficiency compared to legacy architectures, particularly when paired with direct-attached NVMe storage. Because local instance store data is ephemeral, deployments requiring persistence must design around host lifecycle boundaries. This setup is appropriate for compute-heavy, IOPS-sensitive applications such as distributed caching, temporary data crunching, continuous integration builds, and edge batch processing.
description: Amazon Web Services c9gd.large is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by an arm64 AWS Graviton processor. It provides 2 dedicated physical cores clocked at 3.3 GHz alongside 4.0 GB of RAM, sustaining a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio. Distinct from purely network-storage instances, the c9gd.large incorporates a high-speed 118 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume alongside a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. It includes no dedicated GPUs. The combination of dedicated arm64 execution cores and low-latency ephemeral local storage yields strong operational efficiency for tasks that demand rapid scratch space and dedicated CPU processing without hyper-threading contention. The instance is well matched for continuous integration build runners, microservices, batch processing, and temporary caching layers.
